Lautenberg Chemical Safety for the 21st Century Act, EPA has taken action to reduce exposures to certain chemicals that are persistent, bioaccumulative and toxic (PBT). These chemicals build up, or accumulate, in the environment over time and can therefore have potential risks for exposed populations, including the general population, consumers and commercial users, and susceptible subpopulations (such as workers, subsistence fishers, tribes and children). pages.text: Personal Assistance Services | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Personal Assistance Services More in This Section Close Accessible Technology Communications Access Health Care Housing Personal Assistance Services Transportation Universal Design For many individuals with disabilities, personal assistance services (PAS) help make employment possible. Some people use PAS to carry out activities of daily living. Depending on the individual, such activities might include getting up and ready for work, bathing, dressing, cooking, cleaning, or running errands. Some people also use PAS in the workplace. Examples of workplace PAS vary, but may involve activities such as retrieving materials out of reach or providing travel assistance for an employee with a mobility impairment; helping an employee with a cognitive disability in decision-making; reading printed materials to an employee who is visually impaired; or ensuring a sign language interpreter is present during meetings for an employee who is deaf. Whether at home or work, PAS can be essential to employment success. Recognizing this, ODEP works to expand and raise awareness of employment-related PAS options. Meeting the needs of people on and off the job raises important policy issues for federal and state governments, service providers, and employers, as well as people with disabilities themselves. ODEP recognizes PAS is a critical issue — not only for those seeking employment, but also for those already employed. The Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act (LMRDA) establishes reporting and recordkeeping requirements for employers and labor relations consultants. Pursuant to the LMRDA, this agency, the U.S. Department of Labor’s Office of Labor-Management Standards (OLMS), has established the Form LM-10 Employer Report and Forms LM-20 and 21 consultant reports, on which the parties must report concerning agreements or arrangements to persuade employees concerning their rights to organize and bargain collectively or supply an employer with information concerning the activities of employees or a labor organization in connection with a labor dispute involving the employer. An employer must file a Form LM-10 concerning other matters as well, including for expenditures made with an object to commit an unfair labor practice or to obtain information concerning the activities of employees or a labor union involved in a labor dispute. The transparency created by these requirements is designed to better inform workers in making determinations regarding the exercise of their rights to organize and bargain collectively. Pertussis CHIM Biorepository Dec. 2, 2025 Key points Scientists recently developed a pertussis controlled human infection model (pertussis CHIM). The aim was to build a foundation for and accelerate development and licensure of next-generation pertussis vaccines in the United States. Biological samples from this pertussis CHIM are available for researchers. Request samples by following the application process. Overview The first North American pertussis CHIM study began enrolling participants in July 2022. The objective of this study was to establish a pertussis CHIM. Researchers aimed to identify a Bordetella pertussis challenge dose that could safely and reproducibly achieve mild, symptomatic infection in healthy adults aged 18–40 years. The B. pertussis strain (D420) used in this study was a well-characterized strain obtained from a U.S. infant with pertussis. The Canadian Center for Vaccinology, located in Halifax, Canada, established the CDC-supported North American pertussis CHIM platform. Pertussis rates are highest among young children in countries that have lower vaccination coverage. Learn about global trends in pertussis. Global impact Pertussis remains one of the leading causes of vaccine-preventable deaths worldwide, despite overall high vaccination coverage. Most pertussis deaths occur in young babies who are either unvaccinated or incompletely vaccinated . Trends In 2024, the World Health Organization (WHO) reported 941,565 pertussis cases globally. Between 1990 and 2019, the global number of new cases of pertussis annually declined 40.98%. A 2014 publication estimated 24.1 million pertussis cases and 160,700 deaths in children younger than 5 years worldwide. Low vaccination coverage The incidence of pertussis is highest among young children in countries where vaccination coverage is low, primarily in the developing world. Pet Travel Safety Apr. 15, 2026 What to know Plan ahead of time if including pets in your travel plans. Microchip your pet and make sure your contact information is updated. Make sure your pet's vaccinations are up to date. Check regulations and required documentation for your destination before traveling. Preparing for travel with pets Owning a pet can increase opportunities to exercise, get outside, and explore new places. You may want to take your pet with you when you travel to new places. Traveling can sometimes be stressful, both for you and your pets. Preparation can help prevent stress and keep you and your pets safe and healthy. Before traveling, properly identify your pet in case you get separated during your trip. Make sure your pet is microchipped for identification and keep your contact and pet information updated. History In 2010, a paper map by 3dShapes was digitized and imported, to map landuse in Nederland. The import project was well conducted and properly documented in the OSM-wiki. This was a major step in filling in the space on OSM. Some problems remained after import, to be dealt with later. For instance, where trees had been planted in multiple rows, it was imported as an orchard. As a result, our motorways were suddenly lined with orchards, on OSM-based maps. This has been fixed by organized mappings. Another example: the paper map had a tile grid of thin black lines. These lines were seen as cut lines, resulting in unnecessary and awkward splits of the imported areas. The import procedure did detect this problem, but couldn’t automate a fix, so this was left to the future mappers. It took 15 years before a crazy mapper got rid of this in a solo project lasting 2 months. Guess who? The issue Not much of a problem, more of an annoyance, really: All polygons were tagged with “source=3dShapes”. A significant part of the polygons still carry this source tag. pages.title: Peter Storey: Former Arsenal and England midfielder dies aged 81 - BBC Sport
pages.description: Former Arsenal and England midfielder Peter Storey - who helped the Gunners win the Double in 1970-71 - has died at the age of 81.
pages.text: Peter Storey: Former Arsenal and England midfielder dies aged 81 - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Peter Storey won 19 caps for England Published 17 November 2026 Former Arsenal and England midfielder Peter Storey has died at the age of 81. Storey made 501 appearances in all competitions for the Gunners between 1965 and 1977, scoring 17 goals. He was part of the Double-winning Arsenal team which secured the First Division title and FA Cup in 1970-71 under manager Bertie Mee. "Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of double winner Peter Storey," Arsenal said in a statement. "All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time. "We will pay our respects to Peter at our forthcoming home match against Borussia Dortmund." Surrey-born Storey joined Arsenal as an apprentice in 1961 and made his first-team debut against Leicester City in 1965, initially starting his career at right-back before being moved into midfield. He is currently eighth on Arsenal 's list of all-time appearance holders and was capped 19 times by England, although he did not feature in a major tournament for the Three Lions. Storey collected runners-up medals with Arsenal in the League Cup in 1967-68 and 1968-69 and in the FA Cup in 1971-72. He joined Second Division Fulham on a free transfer in March 1977 and made 19 appearances for the Cottagers before his contract was terminated later that year and he retired. The spirit bears are a rare subspecies of black bear, found only along Canada's Pacific coast, with a recessive genetic mutation that causes their ghostlike white fur. And in this unpredictable wilderness, he finds the deepest sense of peace. "It’s always been the reverence I have for nature. I mean, I don’t want to get too religious or anti-religious, but that's my church, and that's where I find everything makes sense,” Nicklen told National Geographic. “I've had nothing but reverence for nature since I was a little kid." Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live What is PHP and why did it spark a global cyber-security scramble? 23 October 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google Liv McMahon , Technology reporter and Osmond Chia , Business reporter How did AI discover the internet's massive cyber-security risk? For more than a decade, serious flaws had gone undetected in the technology underpinning much of the internet. It took AI to bring them to light and caused a global cyber-security alert. Researchers who helped surface the vulnerabilities in PHP - a popular server-side programming language used in web development for decades - warned platforms which use it could be exposed to potential hacks. Governments and cyber-security agencies rushed to contain the fallout , urging website owners to check if their sites were affected and, if so, install updates to patch the issue or consider going offline. There have been no reports of any successful exploits of the flaw, coined php2shell, so far. But in the days since the issues came to light, disruption to sites and services has continued to ripple around the world. What is PHP? Most people may not have heard of PHP, but they probably interact with it daily. It stands for PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor, an open-source, back-end programming language which runs on a web server. Located approximately 100 miles (161 km) northeast of Fairbanks, this 27-mile (44 km) hiking trail traverses a series of alpine ridge tops entirely above timberline. The trail was built for hikers, but is open to all forms of non-motorized use. The Pinnell Mountain Trail is marked with rock cairns as it crosses open tundra with views north to the Yukon River and south to the Alaska Range. Wooden posts along the trail show the mileage from the start at Eagle Summit to the trail's end at Twelvemile Summit. Two shelters provide refuge from storms, but hikers should come prepared for unpredictable, dramatic alpine weather. The Census Bureau has long sought to improve communications with the public, dependent as we are on public cooperation in our censuses and surveys. Public Library Archives Birmingham Civil Rights National Monument was established in 2017, and encompasses roughly four city blocks in downtown Birmingham, Alabama. The National Monument includes the A.G. Gaston Motel, which served as the headquarters for the Birmingham campaign. From April through May of 1963, leaders of the civil rights movement, including Reverend Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr., took up residence at the motel. Here they strategized and made critical decisions about the non-violent campaign that targeted Birmingham’s segregation laws and practices. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Canyons of the Ancients National Monument | Colorado View Map In Full Screen Canyons of the Ancients National Monument, located in the Four Corners region of southwestern Colorado, protects a stunning cultural landscape with the highest known density of archaeological sites in the United States. Encompassing 176,000 acres of public lands, the Monument features more than 8,300 documented sites—including villages, kivas, field houses, cliff dwellings, petroglyphs, and ancient roadways—with estimates suggesting over 30,000 yet to be recorded. These sites offer a window into over 12,000 years of human history, primarily shaped by Ancestral Puebloan cultures and their descendants. The area continues to be a living landscape used today for traditional purposes, recreation, hunting, livestock grazing, and energy development. It also encompasses Cross Canyon , Sego Lily, and Cahone Canyon Wilderness Study Areas. While exploring the Monument’s canyons, mesas, and desert terrain, visitors are reminded to Visit with Respect and Leave No Trace to protect the resources that define this unique place. pages.text: Plant extinctions are shaking Earth’s green foundation | National Geographic Gardeners’ demand for the Chilean crocus nearly drove it extinct in the wild by the 1950s. But in 2001, a thriving population was found on land south of Santiago Photograph By SELECTPHOTO/ALAMY STOCK PHOTO ENVIRONMENT VANISHING Plant extinctions are shaking Earth’s green foundation Compared with birds, mammals, and amphibians, more plants have vanished in the wild since 1900. What’s the cost to ecosystems? By Michael Greshko 3 min read This story appears in the October 2019 issue of National Geographic magazine. When you conjure up “extinction” in your mind’s eye, you probably see an animal—a dodo , perhaps, or a Tasmanian tiger . But the biodiversity crisis isn’t just faunal, it’s floral too. Since the 1750s, at least 571 species of plants have gone extinct in the wild, according to a global survey recently published in Nature Ecology & Evolution . More than eight plant species have disappeared every three years, on average, since 1900. Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine can prevent pneumococcal disease . Pneumococcal disease refers to any illness caused by pneumococcal bacteria. These bacteria can cause many types of illnesses, including: Pneumonia (infection of the lungs) Ear infections Sinus infections Meningitis (infection of the tissue covering the brain and spinal cord) Bacteremia (bloodstream infection) Anyone can get pneumococcal disease, but young children, older adults, and people with certain risk factors are at the highest risk. Most pneumococcal infections are mild. However, some can result in long-term problems, such as brain damage or hearing loss. Pneumococcal Disease in Adults and Vaccines to Prevent It Feb. 25, 2026 Español Key points Pneumococcal disease in adults can range from mild to serious and can sometimes be deadly. Two types of vaccines provide protection against pneumococcal disease. Talk to a healthcare provider to see if they recommend these or any other vaccines for you. Types of infections Pneumococcal disease is a term used for a wide range of infections caused by bacteria called Streptococcus pneumoniae (pneumococcus). Mild infections Ear and sinus infections are examples of the mild infections these bacteria can cause. Although rare, people can have serious infections or complications from ear and sinus infections. Serious infections The following types of pneumococcal disease can be very serious, even deadly: Pneumonia (lung infection) Bacteremia (bloodstream infection) Meningitis (infection of the lining of the brain and spinal cord) View Larger Bacteremia and meningitis are the deadliest types of pneumococcal disease. Pneumococcal Disease Surveillance and Trends Feb. 25, 2026 Key points CDC tracks invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) using 2 surveillance systems. Invasive bacterial disease refers to when bacteria invade parts of the body, like blood, that are normally free from germs. CDC doesn't track non-invasive pneumococcal disease, such as pneumococcal ear infections. Learn about the latest trends in IPD. Data systems National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System Invasive diseases, such as meningitis and bacteremia (bloodstream infections), are the only nationally notifiable diseases caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae bacteria. CDC collects national information about IPD through the National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System (NNDSS). CDC receives NNDSS data each week from state and public health partners. pages.text: Polar Bears in the Roman Colosseum? | National Geographic By Candida Moss Published September 28, 2026 Want to make sure you get every Stones & Bones newsletter? Put your email here . There’s a strange and intriguing reference in the writings of a first-century Roman poet who describes a showdown between bears and seals (or, as he called them, “sea-calves”) in the Colosseum. Only polar bears are known to fight seals, so this raises a question no modern scholar has yet been able to answer: How on Earth would arctic bears have traveled to the heart of the Roman Empire? A clue to the ursine mystery has recently emerged—in the first English language book on Scandinavian Roman-era history, Dagfinn Skre's The Northern Routes to Kingshi p . Skre places Sweden, Norway, and Denmark at the periphery of the empire, showing that Denmark was only a four-week march from the Roman frontier. And in fact, the Roman military was recruiting from the region by the late first century A.D. So the social networks and infrastructure were in place to facilitate the movement of exotic animals that Rome craved for its spectacles. I reached out to Michael Kulikowski, a professor of classics at Penn State who wrote about Skre’s work for the London Review of Books , for more on how polar bears could have ended up on the sands of Rome’s most famous arena. A scum of ash was thickening on the surface of the Gulf of Naples, and black fumes were swallowing the sky above. In a waterfront warehouse in the Roman town of Oplontis, five dozen people cowered in terror. Some clutched gold coins and jewelry—family wealth snatched up in panic. Others gripped common iron tools and little more. One young woman hugged her swollen belly, terrified for the unborn child inside. Their ages and social classes varied widely, but they’d likely all gathered in a storeroom on the water’s edge for the same reason: to await a rescue boat they were increasingly fearful would never come. In A.D. 79, Mount Vesuvius blew its top, raining ash over the Campania region of Italy, near modern-day Naples, and burying surrounding communities beneath as much as 60 feet of volcanic debris. What happened that day in A.D. 79 began with a single event, the eruption of Mount Vesuvius . But each settlement in the volcano’s shadow—including the most famous, Pompeii —experienced a distinct catastrophe depending on its location relative to the volcano and the timing, speed, and direction of the material Vesuvius spewed. Yet, few people pay much attention to the complex systems that keep it flowing. With technology and society in a state of flux, the challenge of providing communities with reliable, efficient sources of power is only getting harder. Renewable energy, electric vehicles, AI-powered data centers, and aging infrastructure are all placing unprecedented pressure on electricity networks that were designed for a very different world. Increasingly, generating power isn't the hardest part—managing it is. For almost 30 years, OATI (Open Access Technology International) has been helping utilities meet that challenge. Pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine (PPSV23) can prevent pneumococcal disease . Pneumococcal disease refers to any illness caused by pneumococcal bacteria. These bacteria can cause many types of illnesses, including: Pneumonia (infection of the lungs) Ear infections Sinus infections Meningitis (infection of the tissue covering the brain and spinal cord) Bacteremia (bloodstream infection) Anyone can get pneumococcal disease, but young children, older adults, and people with certain risk factors are at the highest risk. Most pneumococcal infections are mild. However, some can result in long-term problems, such as brain damage or hearing loss. Pregnancy and Rubella July 11, 2025 Español Key points Rubella is very dangerous for developing babies and can cause congenital rubella syndrome (CRS). Anyone who is not vaccinated against rubella is at risk of getting the disease. You should make sure you are vaccinated against rubella before you get pregnant. Risk factors Rubella is very dangerous during pregnancy If you are planning to get pregnant, you should make sure you are protected against rubella beforehand. Anyone who is not vaccinated against rubella is at risk of getting the disease. If you get rubella during pregnancy, you are at risk for miscarriage or stillbirth. Your developing baby is at risk for severe birth defects with devastating, lifelong consequences. Infection with rubella virus causes the most severe damage during early in pregnancy, especially in the first 12 weeks (first trimester). MMR vaccine protects against rubella Although rubella was declared eliminated from the United States in 2004, cases can occur when unvaccinated people are exposed to infected people.
